# Xenoarchaeology
Xenoarchaeology is a field of science focused on researching alien [bold]artifacts[/bold].
Unlocking their secrets grants research points, raises the artifact's sale value, and reveals strange, potentially useful, or dangerous effects.
Artifacts can be: - Found by mining asteroids around the sector - Bought from miners and salvagers - Assembled from [bold]fragments[/bold]
## Artifacts
Artifacts contain [bold]nodes[/bold] arranged in [bold]layers[/bold], usually in two or three separate clusters. - Each node has [bold]triggers[/bold], actions that must be performed on or near the artifact, and an [bold]effect[/bold]. - Performing a trigger wakes the artifact for a short window. To unlock a node, land [bold]its trigger and the triggers of every node above it[/bold] inside one window. First-layer nodes need only their own. - When a node unlocks, its effect fires [bold]once[/bold]. - Deeper nodes have harder triggers, nastier effects, and are worth more. - Every artifact carries a [color=#a4885c]severity profile[/color]: effects start gentle at the first layer and climb toward a peak class. Some artifacts climb steadily, some spike early then level off, and some stay quiet almost to the end before turning vicious.
## Equipment
- [bold]Artifact Analyzer:[/bold] Stationary pad that scans the artifact resting on it, sending data to the console. - [bold]Analysis Console:[/bold] Displays the node graph, per-node details, and the artifact-wide readout. Must be linked to an analyzer with a network configurator. The [color=#a4885c]Extract[/color] button drains research points from every unlocked node. - [bold]Node Scanner:[/bold] Hand-held device that shows which triggers the artifact has registered while it is awake, so a scientist can work deep chains away from the console.
- [bold]Artifact Container:[/bold] Safely stores and transports artifacts and prevents nodes from triggering.
- [bold]Artifact Crusher:[/bold] Crushes artifacts into fragments. - [bold]Artifact Fragment:[/bold] Pieces of destroyed artifacts. Ten fragments can be rebuilt into a new artifact using the craft menu.
## What an Artifact Is Worth
Every node is worth more the harder it was to solve. A node's value comes from how difficult its trigger is to set up and land inside an unlock window, compounded with how dangerous its effect is to a crew in a sealed hull. A node that makes you vent a compartment while the artifact breaks windows is worth far more than one you examine while it glows.
The console learns its severity readout from your work: unlocking [color=#a4885c]any three nodes[/color] reveals the profile's shape, and reaching a [color=#a4885c]deepest node[/color] reveals the peak severity class.
On top of that, the whole artifact carries an [color=#a4885c]Extraction Bonus[/color]. Every node you unlock compounds it, climbing faster and faster until a fully solved artifact pays out [color=#a4885c]five times[/color] its base worth. The console shows the current bonus.
This applies to Research Points and to the sale price alike. It also means [color=#a4885c]points you extract early are banked at the low bonus and cannot be reclaimed later at the higher rate[/color].
